title: Alice Kern affidavit on Tiger Rag authorship
summary: The reader reads a 1940 sworn affidavit by organist Alice Kern that she wrote down La Rocca's compositions including Tiger Rag.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Archive copyright notices and interviewee headnotes

blocks.x: came and appeared, Mrs. Alice, how do you pronounce her? Alice, Alice Kern. Alice Kern, K-I-E-R-N. A female person over the age of majority and full well known unto me notary public, who first being duly sworn, disposed and said as follows, that deponent was well acquainted with and has personally known for more than 25 years, one Dominic J. La Rocca, who resides in the city of New Orleans, state of Louisiana. A deponent is an organist by profession and during a period of time from 1914 to 1916, set down on paper various compositions originated by the said Dominic J. La Rocca, among which compositions was the number presently known as Tiger Ray, that the said Dominic J. La Rocca originated and played the aforementioned numbers by ear, not knowing the reading and writing of music, and would either play on his cornet or hum the mentioned numbers to deponent, that on the occasion when the said Dominic J. La Rocca first played Tiger Ray to deponent, it was the first time that deponent had ever heard same, and thereupon reduced same to writing, that deponent has always considered the aforementioned Dominic J. La Rocca as the composer and originator of the song, presently known as an entitled Tiger Ray. Signed, Mrs. Alice Kern. Sworn to and subscribed to before me this 12th day of June 1940, David L. Herman, Notre Republic.
